question.problem: Find the volume of the solid region enclosed by the planes $x=1-y$ and $x=y+1,$ and the planes $y=1,$ $y=2,$ $z=0,$ $z=1.$
question.worked_solution:
Notice that our solid can be written as a type II region: 

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,1\le y\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,1-y\le x\le y+1\}
$$

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is given by the following triple integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1-y}^{y+1}\,dx\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}[x]_{x=1-y}^{x=y+1}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}y+1-(1-y)\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}2y\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}2y[z]_{z=0}^{z=1}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}2y\,dy \\  & =[{y}^{2}]_{y=1}^{y=2} \\  & ={2}^{2}-{1}^{2} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$
